newsitem.title: ITALY: More Albanian refugees in Italy, Rome sends aid.
newsitem.headline: More Albanian refugees in Italy, Rome sends aid.

text.p: Hundreds more Albanian refugees arrived in Italy on Monday as Rome sent further emergency medical aid to its Balkan neighbour.
Early on Monday morning a ship with around 350 refugees arrived at the southeast Italian port of Brindisi and another ship with at least 100 others was on its way, the coastguard said.
Nearly 12,000 refugees have arrived in Italy since March 13 to escape the chaos in their country.

A cargo plane with some six tonnes of medical aid was due to arrive at Tirana airport on Monday morning. Two tonnes of emergency were sent by helicopter to the rebel-held southern city of Vlore on Sunday.
Albanian Prime Minster Bashkim Fino was holding talks on Monday afternoon with Prime Minister Romano Prodi to dicuss international aid and the effect the mass exodus has had on Italy.
European Union foreign ministers were meeting in Brussels to work out the details of an aid mission, including who should head a modest police force to secure the mission.
Albania wants police units from abroad to secure ports, roads and railways so that relief supplies can be distributed effectively.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini wants a protection force to prevent the aid falling into the wrong hands but has said a military operation was "not opportune".
Fino will discuss the Albanian crisis with EU Foreign Ministers on Tuesday at a meeting in Rome to mark the 40th anniversary of the founding of the European Economic Community.
